title: League of Legends Patch 26.22 Notes
description: Patch 26.22 is at the top of the charts. K/DA is starting fires, Mel got a midscope, and plenty of changes are in for SR, Mayhem, and Classic.

entries.context: Hooray! TFT is all grown up! They’re officially moving to their own standalone client starting on November 4th, 2026. To accommodate their new home, you can expect this patch to be larger than usual. We are making sure that it’s as easy as clicking a button to swap between League of Legends and Teamfight Tactics whenever you want. Despite this upcoming separation, all existing Teamfight Tactics cosmetics will remain usable in League. The first batch of TFT-only Little Legends will arrive on December 1st, with December 15th marking the date of full separation for TFT cosmetics including emotes and icons. In a future patch, we'll be adding the option to fully opt out of TFT downloads in League patches. To make this possible, 26.22 will be a larger download than usual. For more information, read more here and we’ll see (some of) you on the Convergence!

entries.name: Aurelion Sol
entries.context: The majority of Aurelion Sol players have made it pretty clear that they would much rather rank up his Singularity (E) second over his Astral Flight (W) even though it’s a much weaker second max. We agree that his (E) is a very cool signature spell, so we’re giving him a buff there to help make doing the intuitive fun thing the right thing.

entries.name: Corki
entries.context: We were cautious about Corki’s power level going into Worlds, but now (like Azir and Orianna), he has some more space to be better for everyone.

entries.name: Kayle
entries.context: We've seen Kayle's relevance decrease steadily from earlier this year as the game’s moved past the top lane shake up from role quests. We’re giving her a small bump to help out her early laning since we believe that top lane could use some more scaling options.

entries.name: Locke
entries.context: While Locke's performance in general is within reason, he's proven to be a much deeper champion than we initially expected and players who have reached that level of Locke play have shown him to still be clearly too strong, especially early game.

changes.text: Duration: 6s ⇒ 5s
changes.label: Duration

entries.name: Maokai
entries.context: Maokai has remained a very still tree this year, and has been almost entirely stuck in support. We’re buffing him in a way that helps out his top and jungle more.

entries.name: Mel
entries.context: This patch, Mel is getting a midscope adjustment. You can read more about it here. For the spark notes version, she is having some power moved from early game to scaling, her W is being reworked into an Area-of-Effect missile destruction that retaliates rather than reflects effects, and her Q and R are getting adjustments to lower their cooldowns later on in the game so she can stack her passive to ever higher amounts.

entries.context: After a series of nerfs earlier this year, Naafiri has largely fallen out of mid lane entirely and has been pretty mediocre in the jungle. We’re giving her a buff that should primarily help out her mid, bringing her role power closer to parity.

entries.name: Shen
entries.context: Along with Maokai, Shen jungle has been pushed too far out of the meta. We were watching to see if some of the previous patches’ changes to help jungle tanks would bring him back up, but now we’re confident we can just buff him .

entries.name: Smolder
entries.context: Our buffs a few patches ago landed a bit softer than we expected, but he’s ended up with a good balance between his Crit and Caster builds, so we’re giving him a more generic buff this time. We also expect the Doran’s Bow nerf in this patch to help him out a bit.

entries.name: Thresh
entries.context: Despite our prior nerf, Thresh has remained at the very top of the support pecking order for top tier players, so it’s time for another.

changes.text: Attack Damage: 56 ⇒ 54
changes.label: Attack Damage

entries.name: Viktor
entries.context: Last patch's nerf to Viktor hit him harder than we expected - but we are happy about the impact it had on his early game bullying, so we are buffing him back in scaling.

changes.label: Health Growth

entries.name: Yasuo
entries.context: We were on the fence last patch with whether Yasuo would also need a nerf like Yone, but he's also continued growing in winrate as players migrate to crit builds and banrate reflecting that so he's getting the same treatment.

entries.name: Zaahen
entries.context: Zaahen is living up to his scaling fantasies, but hasn’t had enough to do in lane. This should make his early scrapping and skirmishing much more satisfying.

entries.context: We’re nerfing Doran's Bow by a minor amount, as it’s settled into a spot that is slightly but clearly too strong, resulting in marksmen that we expect to be leaning towards Doran's Blade instead being almost purely Doran's Bow users.

entries.context: Hello Superstars! This patch, we’re lowering the power of some new augments on the scene, buffing some survivability augments, and fixing a bunch of bugs. We’ve been monitoring the explosiveness of combat in the new update and want to alleviate some of the more frustrating situations. Fighters have become exceptionally good at closing out games and poke dominates early in the most recent update while tanks have been struggling. We’re aiming to bring down the power of some of the augments that have been making tanks feel so fragile like Take ‘Em Down Down Down and Weapon of Destiny. We’re also bringing up the power of survivability augments like Soul Eater and Stay Resolute. We're looking at overall burst and game pacing right now to make sure things don’t feel too snowbally. The stage crews have also finished setting up on Butcher’s Bridge and Koeshin’s Crossing so both of those maps will be back in the rotation with Headliner performances. With Worlds in full swing, the last page of the Journey to Stardom is now accessible. Complete all the missions and make your way to the Worlds stage to earn all the rewards! Two new augments are also joining the fray including one based on a classic World’s Anthem that’ll definitely make your enemies remember you. As always, thank you for playing and for all your feedback!

entries.context: Our penultimate content patch arrives with three new old champions to play. Up first, winner of Council Vote #2, Volibear! Run down your enemies, fear nearby minions, and take a bite out of crime. Swain also makes his re-entrance, full of bird-fueled mayhem. And finally, Elise, while not particularly different, has a lot of single-target damage with which to lay waste to her opposition. We’ve also got a bigger balance patch than usual, taking aim at some of the game’s largest outliers on both the top and bottom end. Yes, Janna, your time has come.

entries.name: - Volibear
entries.context: This version of Volibear was active from 2011 to 2018, before his E got the knock-back and anti-dash synergy. He’s a tanky melee fighter who excels in sustained combat before finally dealing a significant burst of damage to low-health enemies.

We fixed the auto-attack bug with a day-1 micropatch but the cooldown change was tooltip only until now.

entries.name: Amumu
entries.context: With bug fixes and balance changes combined, Amumu has wound up as one of the game’s strongest junglers. We’re here to tap him back down to where a straightforward fast-farming jungler is meant to rest. We’re reverting some of our earlier buffs and pulling another one from history to bring down his team-wiping AoE power.

entries.name: Evelynn
entries.context: Evelynn has fallen off as time went on and now looks like one of the weaker junglers, so we’re here to give her a boost. We’re undoing her Hate Spike damage nerf to ensure she can keep up with everyone else.

entries.name: Ezreal
entries.context: AP Ezreal has never quite hit the mark so it’s time for buffs. As AD Ezreal is doing just fine, we’re delivering simple AP ratio buffs and playing up his healer alternate playstyle since it’s so unique to this version of the champion.

entries.name: Fiddlesticks
entries.context: Fiddlesticks, like any good scarecrow, is outstanding in his field. Well, fields. He’s a great jungler and support, so we’re going to prune some power from both. With how much his E’s mana cost goes up with rank, we want to make sure ranking it is valuable, but he otherwise outputs too much damage too quickly.

entries.name: Gangplank
entries.context: Gangplank is still one of the game’s weakest top laners and junglers, so we’re back for more buffs. While some of these may feel a little scattershot, they’re all period-accurate buffs and reverted-nerfs from before his subsequent 2015 rework. The only novel changes here are to his base stats, where we hope to make him more resilient and allow him to play bruiser builds in addition to crit burst.

entries.context: Janna has been an extreme top performer for a while so it’s time to bring her down to size. We aim to keep her global passive intact, but want to make sure it’s not so dominant that it crushes other lanes' interactions.

entries.name: Nami
entries.context: Nami didn’t make the cut for buffs in her initial patch but as time has gone on, she’s floundering. She doesn’t have any historical buffs or nerfs to key into before the Preseason Four support update, so we’re creating some novel changes. In the interest of experimentation, we’re playing up her ability to deal a lot of damage if she can land everything and optimize for it. And hey, how about Mid Nami?

entries.name: Olaf
entries.context: Olaf hasn’t quite kept up with other top laners or junglers so we want to play up his strong sustained damage. As with most of our balance changes, we’re digging up changes from his 2011 and 2012 history.

entries.name: Rammus
entries.context: Rammus is the third of the top-performing junglers, so we’re digging up his past to bring him down to size. The armor nerf should do most of the heavy lifting here, as it impacts both his attack damage and W return damage.
